articleTitle: An overview of GSM data services
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Roaming with Data,
abstract: One key objective for the design of GSM was to provide a system which would provide consistently reliable mobile communications, suitable for both speech and data. The author describes the technical functionality required in GSM to support data services. In particular this is: rate adaptation; radio link protocol; forward error correction; and layer 2 relay. Some examples are included of how Cellnet is presenting the technical capabilities to the market within packaged data products.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: AT&T PersonaLink (SM)-a public network for smart agent PICs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Roaming with Data,
abstract: AT&T PersonaLink service is the first public network in the world to incorporate General Magic's Telescript technology. By incorporating Telescript into the AT&T platform, we are able to process smart agents sent from Personal Intelligent Communicators (PICs) that support the Magic Cap operating system also developed by General Magic. This paper presents an overview of AT&T PersonaLink Service and its use of smart agent technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Roaming with Data,
abstract: The ETSI DECT specification describes a telecommunications system which provides facilities for both cordless speech and data. The first mass market acceptance of DECT products will be for telephony applications, for use in both the home and business. This paper aims to show how, in addition, data services can be provided by DECT and the performance that can be expected. The types of service that can be supported are discussed. For the home user and to a lesser extent the business user, these services will originate or terminate in the low bandwidth, analogue PSTN, although this may gradually be superseded by ISDN. The data rates to be supported will be restricted by the capacity of the PSTN and the available modem technology as well as by DECT: currently V.34 achieves a data rate of 28.8 kbps, this will be taken as the upper limit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Roaming with Data,
abstract: Personal communication networks (PCNs) are already operating in the UK and a few other countries, and new PCNs are planned for commencement of service during the next two or three years in several countries around the world. These networks operate according to the DCS-1800 standard developed by ETSI members. This paper provides a brief overview of the data services which can be supported by PCNs, and goes into a more detailed description of the operation and applications for the data messaging services known as Short Message Service and Cell Broadcast Service.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Roaming with Data,
abstract: Shows some of the trends in portable computing technology which will determine the nature of future portable PC products. The speed of change of technology in the PC market is undiminished as the hardware platforms become capable of running more and more sophisticated yet easy to use software applications. In order to grow the market, manufacturers are producing terminals of greater processing power that can manipulate more natural data forms such as sound and video. Portable computers suffer from the fact that in many areas they are unable to use standard components due to the space and weight constraints imposed by the notebook PC format. The accepted size for a notebook PC is A4 and 3 Kg. Within that format, a manufacturer needs to house the following functions: processor, memory, storage, communications and expansion, battery and power supply, and display.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Roaming with Data,
abstract: Considers the position of dedicated data networks within the complex choice of telecommunications services now facing customers with mobile workforces. RAM Mobile Data Ltd. operates a national mobile data network in the UK, based on Ericsson's 'Mobitex' technology which is now the de facto international standard for wireless data communications worldwide. Topics under discussion include the origins of mobile data, the creation of RAM's Network in the UK and the network's underlying technology. The driving forces behind mobile data, and some of the specific applications, also considered, ending with a look at the future evolution of new markets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trialling GSM data services for the mobile office
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Roaming with Data,
abstract: This paper presents the results of a field trial in which a group of salespeople, with minimal experience of using computers, were provided with mobile computing equipment and access to the GSM data and short message service (SMS) for communications. The trial had three purposes: (1) to evaluate the quality of service provided by the GSM data and SM services and determine whether they provide a significant improvement over the data service provided by analogue cellular networks; (2) to investigate the potential for a personal server/mobile client architecture in which the server provides additional communications services to the mobile client; and (3) to learn about the problems experienced by novice users of mobile services. The trial was carried out in Denmark at the end of 1994.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
